standard_prerequisites.name: The weighted spaces X_{mu,a} and the operator I of the article (definitions in Section 1 and the display def_I of Section 2, printed 2.8)
standard_prerequisites.use: Fix the objects whose continuity is asserted and the first formula of def_I used in the second half of the proof.

core_obligations: Reduce the estimate to a direct integral bound: for z_1 at least zero one writes the operator I as the integral of w over a vertical line and bounds the absolute value by the displayed integral (proof lines 708-711).

Evaluate the integral and read off the gain of one order: the integral of (1 + zeta + |z_2|)^{-mu} equals 1 over ((mu - 1) times (1 + z_1 + |z_2|)^{mu-1}), which is bounded by the same expression with 1 + |z| in place of 1 + z_1 + |z_2|, i.e. the norm in X_{mu-1} (proof lines 711-714).
Cover the remaining half line: for z_1 at most zero one uses the first formula of def_I and argues in the same way (proof line 715).
proof_roadmap: Write I as an integral over a vertical line, bound it by the displayed integral, evaluate that integral to gain one power in the weight and handle the other half line through the first formula of def_I (proof lines 707-716).
task_snapshot.difficulty_reason: The proposition states that for mu greater than one the operator I maps the weighted space X_{mu,a} continuously into X_{mu-1} with an explicit constant (statement lines 700-705). The counted proof, ten lines, is a direct estimate carried out in the span: it writes I as an integral over a vertical line, bounds the modulus by the displayed integral, evaluates the integral to exhibit the gain of exactly one order in the weight, and disposes of the other half line by invoking the first formula of def_I and arguing the same way (proof lines 707-716). It is H2 under the lane rule: the estimate is explicit and checkable, and the span contains no citation command.

proof_roadmap: Rewrite the adjoint through the weighted pairing, bound the pairing by small terms in the parameter, and combine with the elementary estimates listed in the proof to force the vanishing of both components for small parameter (proof lines 3653-3692).

It is H2 under the lane rule: the estimates are displayed and the span contains no citation command.

statement_spans.label: author Proposition environment, source label esti-apriori_disque (statement, source lines 3356-3378)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment, copied from source lines 3382-3554 with the six pipeline blank lines turned into comments (Lead ruling 2026-10-15)

standard_prerequisites.name: The smallness threshold on the parameter and the weighted spaces appearing in the statement, defined in the preceding a priori estimate of the same section (the lemma esti-apriori_plan, printed 4.3)
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the range of the parameter in which the estimate is claimed.

standard_prerequisites.name: The linearised system Mad_lineaire displayed in the statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the system whose solutions are estimated, and the object the contradiction argument is applied to.

core_obligations: Argue by contradiction with a sequence: assume the estimate fails, which produces radii tending to infinity and solutions whose norms are bounded while the right hand side tends to zero, and normalise them so that a fixed norm equals one (proof lines 3382-3400).

Extract compactness: the normalised solutions are bounded in the relevant spaces on compact subsets, so a diagonal extraction gives limits on every compact set, and the limit solves the homogeneous system (proof lines 3400-3500).

Use the steps of the argument to force the limit to vanish: the successive steps of the proof (each displayed as a step environment) bound the limit in the weighted space, in the gradient and in the component along the characteristic direction, and combine them into an integral identity (proof lines 3500-3550).
Reach the contradiction: the combined identity makes the norm of the normalised solutions tend to zero, contradicting the normalisation, which proves the estimate (proof lines 3550-3552).
proof_roadmap: Assume the estimate false, build a normalised sequence of solutions on discs of growing radius, extract limits on compact subsets, and run the steps of the argument to show that the limit vanishes, contradicting the normalisation (proof lines 3382-3554).
task_snapshot.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives an a priori estimate for the linearised system on a disc of radius R with a constant independent of R, under a smallness condition on the parameter (statement lines 3356-3378). The counted proof runs 173 lines and is a multi stage contradiction argument carried out entirely in the span: it builds a normalised sequence from a failure of the estimate, extracts convergent subsequences on compact subsets, shows that the limit solves the homogeneous system, and then runs, through the author's own step environments, the bounds in the weighted space, on the gradient and along the characteristic direction, combining them into an integral identity which forces the norm of the normalised solution to vanish and so contradicts the normalisation (proof lines 3382-3552). It is recorded as H3 rather than H2 because the obligation is a genuine multi stage chain rather than a short argument with one checkable step, and the span contains no citation command.

standard_prerequisites.name: The smallness threshold on the parameter coming from the injectivity lemma of the same section (label adj_inj_plan, printed 4.8)
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the range of the parameter in which existence and the estimate are claimed.

standard_prerequisites.name: The linearised system displayed in the statement (label Mad_lineaire, printed 2.12)
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the system whose solvability, and whose solutions, are at issue.

core_obligations: Reduce onto-ness to injectivity of the adjoint: the system is written in operator form with the linearised operator acting on the pair, and since that operator has compact resolvent, by applying Lax-Milgram to it plus a large constant depending only on the parameter, the Fredholm alternative applies and it suffices to prove that its adjoint is injective (proof lines 3726-3736).

Assume the conclusion false and normalise: this produces radii tending to infinity and pairs solving the system on the corresponding discs with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition (the displayed labelled system), normalised so that the norm of the second unknown plus the norm of the gradient of the first equals one (the displayed labelled normalisation), which is the contradiction hypothesis (proof lines 3737-3750).

Let the limits vanish: arguing as in the earlier a priori estimate of the same section, and since the adjoint is injective by the injectivity lemma, the normalised sequence tends weakly to zero on compact sets (proof line 3753).

Check that the additional terms are small and conclude the contradiction: multiplying the two equations by the two unknowns and integrating by parts over the disc, the two estimates obtained in the earlier proof remain true once the extra terms coming from the difference of the adjoint are shown to contribute a quantity vanishing with the radii; the check is carried out explicitly on the annulus and yields a bound of the form a constant over the square of the inner radius (proof lines 3756-3768).

Existence and estimate: solutions therefore exist for square integrable sources, and the a priori estimate for sources in the weighted spaces of the statement then follows from the earlier a priori estimate of the same section (proof lines 3770-3771).
proof_roadmap: Write the system in operator form, get the Fredholm alternative from the compact resolvent, assume the conclusion to fail and normalise a contradicting sequence, let the weak limits vanish through the earlier disc argument, check explicitly that the extra terms of the adjoint are small on the annulus, and conclude existence together with the estimate taken from the earlier a priori lemma (proof lines 3726-3771).
task_snapshot.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts existence of a solution pair in the two Sobolev spaces for source terms in the weighted spaces of order two plus sigma prime and one plus sigma prime, together with an estimate whose constant is independent of the radius and of the sources and whose right hand side carries those source norms plus a term of order one over the square of the parameter applied to the combination of the two source components, in the space of order one plus sigma prime (statement lines 3702-3724). The counted proof runs 46 lines and carries its argument inside the span: it puts the system into operator form, obtains compactness of the resolvent from Lax-Milgram and hence the Fredholm alternative, assumes the conclusion to fail, normalises the resulting sequence, shows the weak limits vanish through the argument of the earlier estimate together with the injectivity of the adjoint, verifies explicitly on the annulus that the additional terms introduced by the adjoint are small, and then reads off existence together with the estimate of the earlier a priori lemma (proof lines 3726-3771). Two steps are compressed by the author with the phrases arguing as for the proof of the earlier estimate and the remaining of the proof is quite similar to it; the card records that compression, and notes that the span nevertheless carries the operator reduction and the explicit annulus estimate. It is H2 under the lane rule: the reductions and the estimate are displayed, and the span contains no citation command.
